newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Mkt calmer but downtrend seen resuming.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Mkt calmer but downtrend seen resuming.

text.p: The GDR market steadied on Tuesday after its flamboyant start to the week, with thin volume and little investor interest, traders said.
"Yesterday's volatile trading, when the market closed up 29 points after falling over 100 points, indicates the turmoil between the bulls and the bears," said one.

"The bears seemed to be winning today with the market resuming its downward move. The BSE (Bombay Stock exchange) 30 index's psychological 3,000 level breaking down again seems to suggest that the year's low of 2,826 on January 25 may be tested before the year end."
Traders said interest was mostly from market-makers.

The BSE closed 44.40 points or 1.48 percent down at provisional 2950.58. ITC shares swung between a low of 273.50 rupees and a high of 289.25 as investors squared positions after the firm's H1 results. The GDR ended down at $8.75. Most other major GDR counters were off their Monday close. Grasim was at $14.0 (14.1), India Hotels at $22.5 (23.0), Tata at $10.7 (11.250), Bajaj Auto at $29.5 (30.6), Hindalco at $18.4 (18.65) and Reliance at $11.35 (11.875). H1 results from India Hotels were broadly in line with expectations and there was interest in telecom firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) which said its GDR issue is now planned for February 1997, filling the slot vacated by Italian telecoms firm STET, which is postponing its own international offer.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI was at 59.52 at 1630 GMT, down 0.96 points or 1.58 percent, with the premium over the local market at 16.70 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index was at 65.13 points, down 0.29 point or 0.44 percent, with a premium at 4.94 percent. The Taiwan GDR Index was off 0.95 percent at 95.36, with a premium of 28.68 percent.
